title: Brokered kernel matchmaker with micro-profiling for mixed-length attention workloads
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Introduce a lightweight 'kernel broker' layer that assigns kernels per-request based on a short micro-profile probe and a compact affinity score. Target mixed sequence-length traffic where a single static kernel choice causes tail latency or cost regressions. The broker should make low-overhead per-request kernel recommendations before full scheduling (prefill) and adapt online using a regret-limited exploration policy.
background: Current runtime selects kernels using coarse heuristics tied to batch size, model family, and device type. For workloads with variable prefill lengths and attention patterns (e.g., chat interleaving short queries and long context synthesis) the chosen kernel often misfits and we see 5-30% tail latency regressions and suboptimal GPU utilization. Existing autotuners perform offline experiments or long-running bandit processes that are too heavy for per-request heterogeneity.
objectives: 1) Reduce 95th percentile latency for mixed-length workloads by 15% compared to static kernel selection. 2) Keep per-request broker overhead under 2ms on average. 3) Ensure no more than 1% additional token cost due to exploratory probes. 4) Provide metrics to quantify broker decisions and rollback events in the Console.
proposed_solution: Design a tiny micro-prober that executes a fast, architecture-safe microbenchmark (memory-touch + small attention kernel simulation) or uses a prefill shadow pass to collect tokenization and KV cache signature. Compute an affinity score combining: (a) estimated memory footprint, (b) attention sparsity proxy, (c) device occupancy prediction. The kernel broker matches affinity -> kernel candidates using a compact fingerprint table; it applies a lightweight cost model to select a winner and a backup kernel. Exploration: randomized epsilon-greedy with decaying epsilon per fingerprint bucket; rollbacks if latency or OOM risk exceeds thresholds.
milestones: M1: Proto micro-prober library with synthetic microbench kernels (2026-03-13)
M2: Broker affinity schema and fingerprint table design (2026-03-16)
M3: Integrate broker into prefill path with opt-in flag (2026-03-20)
M4: Canary on dedicated dev cluster + metrics dashboard (2026-03-24)
M5: Controlled rollout and A/B analysis across chat workloads (2026-03-30)
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency improvement >= 15% vs baseline on representative mixed-length workload (benchmark suite link in references)
Average broker overhead < 2ms measured across canary traffic
Exploratory probe token cost < 1% measured over 48h
Broker exposes per-decision telemetry (reason, fingerprint, chosen_kernel, fallback, latency, memory_estimate) to Console
Rollback triggers correctly bail to safe kernel without OOMs in canary
risks: Probing may increase token usage when implemented as shadow prefill; mitigate via lightweight simulation or capped probe budget
Affinity collisions causing noisy buckets and slower convergence; mitigate with secondary hashing and LRU eviction
Device-specific microbenchmarks may be brittle across driver/kernel upgrades; include calibration step and version fingerprinting
Increased codepath complexity could harm stability; start as opt-in and gate behind feature flag
